text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Israeli forces stormed the self-rule area in Ramallah after an armed confrontation with the Palestinian police.

- President Hosni Mubarak told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that the way to stop violence in the West Bank was to fulfil its agreements with the Palestinians, starting with redeployment in the town of Hebron.
Netanyahu called Mubarak from Paris to ask him to help calm down the situation after Israeli troops killed five Palestinians and injured up to 300 in the Ramallah area.

- The council of regional governors took important decisions to deal with the problems of traffic and cleanliness. It also followed up the decision to provide 23,000 sports grounds in the provinces. It agreed to allow private minibus companies.

- Informed sources told al-Ahram that two of the militants wanted for trying to kill Mubarak in Addis Ababa last year had killed their colleague, Ezzat Yassin, in Khartoum after disagreements with him. One of the militants, Mustafa Hamza, then fled to Afghanistan while the other man, Hussein Shomait, fled to Kenya and later drowned off the Kenyan coast.
- Domestic air fares will go up 15 percent with effect from October 1.
- A Giza court suspended implementation of the ruling which separated academic Nasr Abu Zeid from his wife.
- Palestinian uprising against Netanyahu. Netanyahu asked Mubarak to intervene to calm down the situation.

- Farmers are increasingly keen to deliver their cotton harvest to market at the guaranteed price, which is higher than the world market price. So far they have delivered 325,000 qantars (16,250 tonnes) in 11 provinces.
- The murderer of Rod el-Farag has fallen. Police arrested him at his house and he confessed to killing eight people.
- Mubarak has called for immediate implementation of the Palestinian-Israeli agreements. Netanyahu asks the president to calm the situation down.
- In New York Foreign Minister Amr Moussa warned against Israel contining to escalate the tense situation in the West Bank, especially after the latest clashes.

- The head of the Illegal Gains Department at the Ministry of Justice has frozen the assets of Abdelwahhab el-Habbak, the former chairman of the Holding Company for Engineering Industries. The decision covers the assets and property of his wife and three children.
